races.name: Pentraeth Subaru Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: My Noble Lord
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Greenall & Guerriero, who are 1/3 in the 14-day window; won over this C&D trip in Good last time out but the style-fit flag (0.92) is a mild caution if the race shape demands more than straightforward pace-setting — tongue-tie fitted, 42 days off.|

runners_data.name: Presentandcounting
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 12-year-old brings exceptional Good-ground credentials with 14 of 15 qualifying runs on similar going and two wins plus nine places in that sample; hold-up style suits the expected race shape, Theo Gillard takes over, and 51 days since last run is not alarming at his age.|

runners_data.name: Country Park
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr rides for his father's stable, which is 0/12 in the 14-day window — a stat worth noting; a genuine hold-up horse on Good ground (9 from 14 qualifying runs) but without a win in that sample, and the P headgear first-time hood flags a trainer looking to sharpen focus.|

runners_data.name: Le Gentleman
runners_data.note: Won over the identical trip on Good last time out for Greenall & Guerriero, who have the most live runners in this race; his natural pace means he wants to be prominent, but with My Noble Lord controlling the front, he is effectively denied that role — the style-fit score of 0.93 reflects a horse whose best chance depends on getting a position the race shape may not allow.|

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: Non-runner alert — listed jockey is marked NON-RUNNER so a late jockey change is required before assessment of that angle is possible; an 11-year-old prominent racer with two Good-ground wins from 15 similar runs, and the tp headgear (tongue-tie and hood) suggests connections are managing him carefully at this stage of his career.|

races.paceDynamic: My Noble Lord is the confirmed front-runner here and, with Lermoos Legend and Le Gentleman also carrying prominent styles, there is genuine early pace in this five-runner field — but My Noble Lord is the only horse truly guaranteed to lead, meaning the fractions should be sustainable rather than frenetic. Lermoos Legend is the most likely of the prominent types to actually secure a position close to the pace, given Le Gentleman has been redistributed to midfield on the map as it cannot hold its natural position with My Noble Lord dictating. The result is a race likely run at a measured, honest tempo on Good ground over 2m4½f — not a dawdle, but nothing that will burn off the hold-up horses prematurely. This shape favours horses that travel smoothly just off the pace and have the class to finish, with Presentandcounting and Country Park best positioned to exploit the honest but uncontested gallop My Noble Lord sets. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their natural position, and My Noble Lord is the clear pace-setter with Lermoos Legend the next most likely to press close; Le Gentleman is effectively racing out of role.

scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If My Noble Lord sets a fair, uncontested gallop and the hold-up horses get a clean run from two out.
scenarios.body: If My Noble Lord sets a fair, uncontested gallop and the hold-up horses get a clean run from two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If My Noble Lord and Lermoos Legend push the pace enough to sap the closers' finishing kick.
scenarios.body: If My Noble Lord and Lermoos Legend push the pace enough to sap the closers' finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Flat
scenarios.trigger: If the pace drops away mid-race and My Noble Lord is never truly pressed, turning it into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If the pace drops away mid-race and My Noble Lord is never truly pressed, turning it into a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers thin the field and the race degenerates into a test of jumping accuracy over fitness.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or fallers thin the field and the race degenerates into a test of jumping accuracy over fitness.

watchPoints.text: My Noble Lord is the lone confirmed pace-setter — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the race could set up perfectly for the hold-up horses and his winning chance may be overstated at a short price.
Lermoos Legend is a non-runner regarding jockey — confirm the replacement rider before race-off as any late booking significantly changes confidence in that runner's tactical execution.

Le Gentleman cannot get his natural prominent position with My Noble Lord in the field; watch for Jack Tudor making an early move to try to manufacture a forward berth, which could inject unexpected pace into the first mile.

Country Park has shown zero wins from nine Good-ground runs in the sample — consistency without a win at this trip and going combination suggests a place proposition more than a winning one unless race shape is perfect.

Presentandcounting's age (12) and 51-day absence make the first fence or two a key early watch point — if he jumps cleanly in the opening stages, his experience and Going record move him firmly into play.

races.name: Wrexham Evening Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Slaney Opera
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with strong similar-going profile (8/10 runs, 1W5P), meets her rivals fresh off 32 days and carries 168lbs, but Nick Scholfield's stable is winless in 8 over 14 days — the key tactical asset here is her uncontested lead; tongue-tie reported.

runners_data.name: Dazzlelikethis
runners_data.note: Returning after a 224-day absence (32 days since a point), wearing a hood, and has only one placing from six runs on going this good — the fresh-horse angle is interesting for Jack Tudor but the ground form is a significant concern.

runners_data.name: Glenmalure Flyer
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride on a horse back after 570 days off; all five historical runs show finishes between 6th and 10th at 16-17f, and the "fades in finish" flag is a direct warning over this stiff 3m — the De Bromhead yard has placed 5 from 40 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Vinnie O'Neil
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning (0W0P), genuine hold-up horse who maps to his natural position in the rear group; form shows mid-pack finishes on Good and Soft, and Sam Allwood has only one runner in 14 days — needs something to go wrong up front.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form record (13/15 on Good, four places at this trip), an 11-year-old who gets to his spot from deep under Brendan Powell — though his natural hold-up style is squeezed here by the overcrowded rear, his consistency on this ground makes him the most dangerous of the compressed closers.

runners_data.name: Est Illic
runners_data.note: Twelve-year-old wearing a visor, with three recent places at this trip on Good ground for Sarah-Jayne Davies; James Best takes the ride and he's a true hold-up type forced to run from a mid-field map position — his best chance comes only if the front end weakens dramatically.

runners_data.name: Henry Box Brown
runners_data.note: Unseated last time out is a red flag over fences, and his five-run history on similar going shows 0W4P without a win; true hold-up runner operating closer than he'd like under a 5lb claimer (Ellis Collier), which adds execution risk on top of the jumping concern.

runners_data.name: Radharc Na Slaine
runners_data.note: Best tactically placed of any non-front-runner — prominent style, 13/15 on Good, 1W5P, and form includes a win at 22f on similar ground; Conor Ring navigating from a tracking position behind Slaney Opera makes this horse the most naturally suited to the race shape.

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: Returned from a break just 15 days ago and ran a placed effort (2nd) at 21f on Good; Robert Dunne on a genuine hold-up type who is mapped mid-field — the 3m trip is a stretch in distance terms and his chance depends on pace collapse rather than positional advantage.

runners_data.name: Shuile Warrior
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 73), carrying 143lbs under a 5lb claimer (Paddy Hanlon), with only 1 run from 5 on similar going — deep hold-up style compressed into a midfield slot makes this a very difficult winning profile to construct.

races.paceDynamic: Slaney Opera is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap chase over 3m at Bangor, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should establish a comfortable, sustainable gallop from the outset — Good ground at Bangor rewards precisely this kind of uncontested rhythm over a stamina trip. Radharc Na Slaine is the likeliest horse to track prominently from second position, while the bulk of the field — Dazzlelikethis, Glenmalure Flyer, Vinnie O'Neil and others — will settle in behind, likely in a compact bunch given the single-pace scenario. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Friends Don't Ask, Est Illic, Henry Box Brown, Rockvale and Shuile Warrior are all genuine hold-up performers who are unlikely to secure their natural deep position and will be forced to race closer than ideal, diluting their finishing threat. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a sensible pace on Good ground over a long trip — distinctly favours prominent-racing types who can track the tempo comfortably and pounce in the straight, rather than true closers who will be unable to find clear daylight from a falsely compressed rear group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slaney Opera Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Slaney Opera secures the lead uncontested and sets a honest but not excessive gallop, allowing her to control the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Slaney Opera secures the lead uncontested and sets a honest but not excessive gallop, allowing her to control the tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Slaney Opera and Radharc Na Slaine build a meaningful advantage on the field and the hold-up contingent cannot bridge the gap from three out.
scenarios.body: If Slaney Opera and Radharc Na Slaine build a meaningful advantage on the field and the hold-up contingent cannot bridge the gap from three out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Slaney Opera goes too hard early on Good ground and the pace collapses from three out, creating a genuine late-run opportunity.
scenarios.body: If Slaney Opera goes too hard early on Good ground and the pace collapses from three out, creating a genuine late-run opportunity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Jumping Errors Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If one or more front-runners make costly jumping errors on the chase fences, scrambling the race order and creating an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: If one or more front-runners make costly jumping errors on the chase fences, scrambling the race order and creating an unpredictable finish.

watchPoints.text: Slaney Opera and Radharc Na Slaine — if these two break clear of the pack from the second last, the hold-up contingent crammed in the midfield will have no realistic path to them on Good ground.
Henry Box Brown unseated last time over fences — watch his jumping in the early stages, particularly at the open ditches, as any error could trigger disruption across the tightly bunched field.

Glenmalure Flyer returning after 570 days — monitor whether Harry Skelton settles him early; a fresh horse can easily overrace and compromise the finishing positions of those tracking immediately behind.

Friends Don't Ask carries the strongest Good-ground form profile among the hold-up group (13/15, four places) — if he manages to get a clear run from three out he is the most likely late challenger, despite racing closer than ideal.

The trainer statistics for this race are weak across the board — Scholfield (0/8 in 14 days), Allwood (0/1), Davies (0/5), Rees (0/3) — meaning jockey execution and race-day tactics carry more weight than stable momentum in framing the outcome.

races.name: Wrexham Lager Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
Bangor-On-Dee Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Supreme Yeats
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's ten-year-old has won back-to-back on Good ground over 2m6f and arrives in fine nick off just 13 days; he is the natural front-runner here and gets a dream small-field setup, though his OR of 115 is the highest in the race and he races off the front — a profile that works well when uncontested but the STYLE_FIT tag is a marginal concern if Crystal Glance decides to race more aggressively alongside.

runners_data.name: Il Va De Soi
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's eight-year-old has won his last two starts both on Good ground over 2m1f, which is shorter than today's 2m3½f trip, and he is a genuine hold-up type who needs a strong enough gallop to close into; with only four runners and a likely leader in Supreme Yeats who will control the fractions, the pace may not be honest enough to play to his strengths despite the positive recent form.

runners_data.name: Crystal Glance
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with five wins on Good ground and a good record at this sort of trip, last seen winning 34 days ago; Jack Tudor rides with intent and this horse is drawn to prominent positions naturally, making him the most credible challenger to Supreme Yeats if he decides to race aggressively from the front rather than sit just off the pace.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards's ten-year-old holds four second-place finishes in his recent form but has been posted P on the field map only notionally — he is a genuine prominent type who cannot get that position with Supreme Yeats and Crystal Glance already ahead of him; the 70-day absence, a form string ending in a pull-up, and recent soft-ground runs all represent material concerns on today's Good going.

races.paceDynamic: Supreme Yeats is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Crystal Glance as a likely companion in the early stages, he faces minimal pressure and should control a measured, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m3½f trip on Good ground. Crystal Glance has the form and style to press forward and could race alongside Supreme Yeats, but with Dan Skelton's ten-year-old having the higher OR and a clear front-running habit, Supreme Yeats is the one most likely to dictate terms. Il Va De Soi is a genuine hold-up type who will be anchored at the rear, while Summergrounds — a natural prominent racer — is mapped to midfield here because the front two have already claimed the prominent positions, meaning he cannot get his preferred berth. The field contains more forward-going intent than it can accommodate, with Supreme Yeats and Crystal Glance the likeliest to secure the front, leaving Summergrounds unable to race where he wants; this race shape — steady pace, no real pressure on the leader, small field — most favours a horse that can track from a handy position and sustain a run from two out, with front-runners and close-order types holding a structural edge over hold-up horses who will find the pace insufficient to generate a meaningful late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Supreme Yeats Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Supreme Yeats gets a clean break and dictates an uncontested gallop at his own tempo.
scenarios.body: If Supreme Yeats gets a clean break and dictates an uncontested gallop at his own tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Crystal Glance Pressures And Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Crystal Glance pushes Supreme Yeats harder than expected, setting an honest pace that suits a finishing challenge.
scenarios.body: If Crystal Glance pushes Supreme Yeats harder than expected, setting an honest pace that suits a finishing challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Il Va De Soi Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough that the leaders tie each other up and Il Va De Soi finds a rare finishing surge.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough that the leaders tie each other up and Il Va De Soi finds a rare finishing surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Summergrounds Finds His Feet
scenarios.trigger: If Supreme Yeats or Crystal Glance makes a costly jumping error that disrupts the front and allows a reshuffling of positions.
scenarios.body: If Supreme Yeats or Crystal Glance makes a costly jumping error that disrupts the front and allows a reshuffling of positions.

watchPoints.text: Supreme Yeats has a tongue-tie (tb) and if that affects his breathing under pressure from Crystal Glance late on, Crystal Glance is the immediate beneficiary in a two-horse finish.
Summergrounds has not raced for 70 days and his last run ended in a pull-up — watch the parade ring closely for any signs of physical wellbeing before the race begins.

Il Va De Soi's last five runs are all over 2m1f or shorter; if the extra half-mile proves beyond him today, watch for him to stop quickly after the last and confirm the trip is a concern at this level.

With only four runners, any jumping error by Supreme Yeats at the downhill hurdles on the back straight could immediately hand Crystal Glance a lead he would not relinquish — Supreme Yeats's jumping reliability is a key variable throughout.

Crystal Glance's trainer Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero yard is running at 5/21 over the last 14 days — a moderate strike rate, but the horse arrives on the back of a win and Jack Tudor's positive style could see him test Supreme Yeats earlier than the market expects.

races.name: Rachel Jones Memorial Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Into Battle
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse with solid Good-ground form (2W5P in similar conditions), Robert Dunne rides for a small trainer on a 42-day break; best placed when given a clear late run and the uncontested pace set by Centurion's Sister suits his profile perfectly.

runners_data.name: Centurion's Sister
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards sends her back quickest (1/4 T14) and she has consistent placed form on Good ground, but her STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects she is operating outside her natural role as a prominent racer if forced to lead; should control the race but her record shows 0 wins from 8 similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Evening Tess
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old is in sharp form (three places from last five including a recent win), Harry Skelton takes the ride, and the trainer is firing at 13/23 over 14 days — the most potent handler angle in the race; Good ground suits (1W3P in similar) and her hold-up style is ideally matched to the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's gelding holds genuine hold-up credentials backed by tongue tie, but the redistribution means he will be tracking closer to midfield than suits; 52 days off the track is notable and his record of 1W4P on similar ground suggests a place-getter rather than winner.

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Two wins from last two runs on Good ground are eye-catching for Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero, but her natural closing style is compressed into a midfield berth here because the map is already crowded at the rear; Jack Tudor rides but a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and the lightest weight (149lbs) in the race mean she will need everything to fall her way.

races.paceDynamic: Centurion's Sister is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and should dictate from the outset over the 2m½f trip at Bangor, setting a sustainable, uncontested pace on Good ground. With no genuine rival to press her early, she is likely to bowl along at her own rhythm, controlling fractions from the front and giving nothing away. The field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — American Empire and Prettylady are true closers who will be mapping closer to midfield than their natural positions, meaning their finishing kicks may arrive from a less-than-ideal starting point. This race shape — a lone front-runner dictating a measured, fair gallop on Good ground — strongly favours hold-up horses with a clean late run, provided they are genuine closers rather than horses redistributed into that role; Evening Tess and Into Battle, as natural hold-up types, are best placed to exploit a flat-out dash for home in the final stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centurion's Sister Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Centurion's Sister leads uncontested and sets a fair, even gallop that keeps the hold-up horses honest throughout.
scenarios.body: If Centurion's Sister leads uncontested and sets a fair, even gallop that keeps the hold-up horses honest throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace drifts slightly too slow early, compressing the field and setting up a sprint finish that genuine hold-up types can exploit from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace drifts slightly too slow early, compressing the field and setting up a sprint finish that genuine hold-up types can exploit from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Crumbles, Front Runner Weakens
scenarios.trigger: If Centurion's Sister overcooks the gallop or makes a jumping error, leaving the door open for chasers to sweep past.
scenarios.body: If Centurion's Sister overcooks the gallop or makes a jumping error, leaving the door open for chasers to sweep past.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Redistributed Movers
scenarios.trigger: If Prettylady or American Empire push forward early from their mapped midfield positions and disrupt the expected single-leader dynamic.
scenarios.body: If Prettylady or American Empire push forward early from their mapped midfield positions and disrupt the expected single-leader dynamic.

watchPoints.text: Evening Tess — watch whether Harry Skelton finds a clear passage turning for home; if Centurion's Sister slows the pace and Evening Tess gets a clean run two out, she has the form and fitness to win.
Centurion's Sister — monitor her jumping under pressure; if she makes an error at a critical flight on the final circuit her uncontested lead advantage evaporates quickly on this track.

American Empire — 52 days off the track combined with a redistribution into a non-natural position creates a dual concern; watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the early exchanges that could leave Gillard with too much to do.
Prettylady — her two recent wins may attract market support, but punters should note she is not in her natural position in this race shape and her chance is materially lower than raw form suggests.

Into Battle — 42 days since last run for a small trainer (0/5 T14) is a minor flag, but his Good-ground record is strong and Robert Dunne is an experienced handler of hold-up horses in small fields; worth monitoring in-running positioning.

races.name: Tom Jones Live At Chester Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Collingham
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with solid course form on good ground over similar trips, last ran 213 days ago which raises fitness questions, but the sim-going record of 4 wins and 5 places in 15 good-ground runs is genuinely strong and makes him a player if arriving fresh and well.

runners_data.name: Roxboro River
runners_data.note: Ran just 14 days ago and has been consistently placed in good-going contests, but the form string of 40-747 suggests he finds it hard to win and his trainer's 0 from 24 in the last 14 days is a sharp negative angle to note.

runners_data.name: Rock Hurley
runners_data.note: Donald McCain sends out a horse with a recent third over this trip on good ground, but he is a true hold-up type now mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — his best recent form has come on soft, and his good-going sim record of just 1 place from 3 runs tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Innisfree Lass
runners_data.note: The sole pace-maker in this field and the structural pivot of the entire race shape; her form is built on soft ground and she has never shown strong sim-going figures, but Joey Ramsden has two winners from 12 in 14 days and the tp headgear suggests she has been managed for this moment.

runners_data.name: Golden Glance
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 2m on good ground and is trained by Greenall & Guerriero who are 0/3 in 14 days, but her natural hold-up style is squeezed toward midfield here — her good-ground win gives her a form claim yet the style displacement means she won't be in her rhythm until late.

runners_data.name: Jay Bee Whiskey
runners_data.note: Returns from a long absence (584 days including a pulled-up run) and has only one sim-going run to reference, making her form profile deeply uncertain; her natural hold-up style is redistributed to midfield here, and the tp headgear and lightweight (154lbs) don't fully compensate for the fitness query.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with an unknown (U) style tag offering genuine positional flexibility, she ran second on good ground last time out and her youth and light weight (145lbs) are assets; Megan Bevan's 8lb claim helps further and she looks the most adaptable horse in the field to whatever shape emerges.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: Back quickly after just 13 days and has placed twice in eight good-ground runs, so the going suits, but as a true hold-up type remapped to midfield and OR 74, he is the least exposed runner here yet faces the challenge of racing out of his comfort zone over a trip he may not fully see out.

races.paceDynamic: Innisfree Lass is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 2m7f handicap hurdle and, with no horse likely to seriously challenge for the lead, she should settle into a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good ground at Bangor. This creates a single-file, processional shape where the pace is unlikely to be truly searching until the home turn, gifting the leader a potential energy advantage into the closing stages. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Rock Hurley, Golden Glance, Jay Bee Whiskey, and The Kings Soldier are all natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield positions on the map, meaning their redistribution reduces the authenticity of any late-closer scenario. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in a close-tracking position behind Innisfree Lass, as the lack of genuine pace pressure rewards those who are comfortable making their effort from second or third, not those forced to launch a wide, sustained challenge from further back.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Innisfree Lass bowls along uncontested and no rival has the tactical agility to close the gap before the last two hurdles.
scenarios.body: If Innisfree Lass bowls along uncontested and no rival has the tactical agility to close the gap before the last two hurdles.

scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travels smoothly in second or third throughout and picks up strongly after the last when Innisfree Lass tires.
scenarios.body: If a horse travels smoothly in second or third throughout and picks up strongly after the last when Innisfree Lass tires.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes slightly more honest mid-race through sustained pressure from the remapped midfield horses and the winner comes from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace becomes slightly more honest mid-race through sustained pressure from the remapped midfield horses and the winner comes from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If Innisfree Lass makes a serious jumping error or capitulates early, turning the race into a messy, contested scramble.
scenarios.body: If Innisfree Lass makes a serious jumping error or capitulates early, turning the race into a messy, contested scramble.

watchPoints.text: Innisfree Lass — if she jumps poorly at an early hurdle or her lack of good-ground form catches up with her, the entire race shape collapses and all form guides become redundant.

Golden Glance and Rock Hurley — both true hold-up horses pushed into midfield on the map; watch whether either actually settles back to their natural position at the rear, which would leave them with a mountain to climb over 2m7f on a galloping track.

Jay Bee Whiskey — returning from effectively a two-year absence with a pulled-up run in between; even with tp headgear, watch for any signs of blowing up after the halfway point that could cause interference to runners around her.

Athena's Dream — the only horse in the field with a genuinely flexible style tag; watch how jockey Megan Bevan (8lb claimer) positions her in the first mile, as getting her into second or third early would maximise her chance in the dominant scenario.

Roxboro River — Irish-trained raider running just 14 days after his last start; his trainer's cold form (0/24 in 14 days) is a flag, and watch whether Paddy Hanlon settles him quietly at the rear, as a hold-up horse on a day when hold-up types are structurally disadvantaged needs a near-perfect trip to matter.
